body.p: Burujdak. There was a man. This man had the name Burujdak. This man was like a child. It was a rich man. Every day he stood up early in the morning. Every day he bowed to Mugdi.[DCh]: According to RKM (footnote 1), "Mugdi" is a deity of the relevant Evenki clan. One day Burujdak stood up early in the morning. Having stood up he bowed to Mugdi, then he went off. [Over] the whole land was fog. Burujdak thinks: "Why is this?" Then Burujdak looked at the fog, having looked he went back to the tent. Having gone he thought: "What's that for a fog? Why is this?" Then he came to the tent, Burujdak sat down and again started to think. Burujdak thought so: "I'll put on an iron overcoat, iron shoes and an iron cap! I'll make eight bows to the spirit Majin, then I'll go! I'll get to know what this fog is!" Having thought Burujdak took an iron overcoat, iron shoes, an iron cap and put it on. Having dressed he went off, Burujdak went on fur skis. Burujdak was going and going, he saw nothing, he got nothing to know. At one place Burujdak saw the trace of an elk. Having seen [it] Burujdak poked with a stick in the snow, is it solid or soft? Having poked Burujdak ran on fur skis after the elk. Burujdak thought: "The spirit Majin gave success! I'll hunt the elk!" Burujdak ran quickly along the moose's sled. The snow was solid and soft. [At] one place the snow was fluffy. Burujdak saw the elk. Having seen the elk Burujdak set on a blunt arrow. The arrow stuck in the elk's back. It [= the arrow(?)] fell into the elk.[DCh]: According to the original translation the elk fell down, but then DAT/LOC marking seems implausible. Burujdak broke forty trees, then he lit a fire. Having lit a fire Burijdak came to the elk. He cut out the elk's heart. Having cut out the heart he went back to the bonfire. Then he is about to fry the heart. Having fried the heart Burijdak saw a human. He doesn't see well what kind of human is coming. Burujdak is looking again, he was looking, looking well and saw, this human is apparently a woman, a woman is coming. The woman had a stick, a red stick. Burijdak doesn't eat the heart, he is looking at the woman. Then the woman came closer. Burijdak is looking again, having looked he thought: "What a good woman! The spirit Majin has given me today success!" The woman came to Burijdak and says: "Give me a bit of meat!" Burijdak doesn't look at the woman, he won't give meat. The woman got very angry, having got angry she said: "I don't bow to you! I am a werebeast. I'll shapeshift a hundred times! I have food, [I have] an overcoat! You're a fool!" So the woman said, then she quickly went off. Burijdak is surprised: "What's that for a woman? The woman laughed about me. I am a man! I'll find this woman! Now I'll chase [her]!" So Burijdak thought, having thought he went off. On the way Burujdak is thinking again: "I'll find that woman on the earth, I'll grab her at the back! I'll find that woman up [there], I'll grab her at the tail(?)!" Burijdak searched the woman for a long time. He was searching and searching, he saw the trace of a mouse. Having seen the trace of the mouse, he went along the trace. He was going, going, going and he chased the mouse. The mouse saw the man and shapeshifted, it turned into a woman. The woman said: "Go back, man! Your back [will] be like that of a hare! You won't outrun me!" So the woman said, then she went off quickly. Burijdak heard to the woman's words, having listened he got angry and thought: "You're lying, you dog! I'll outrun you! I am a man!" So Burijdak thinks, then he again is chasing the woman. For a long time Burijdak is looking for the woman. He was searching the woman for three years. Burijdak dried out like a hare, he is hungering. He lost his power. He lost his power, he fell against a tree. A raven came flying. The raven sat down on the top of tree and sang: "Caw caw! That's good! I'll peck the eyes [out]! I'll peck the brain [out]! I'll eat fresh meat! I'll eat the joints! I'll drink hot blood!" So the raven sang. Having sung it flew off. Having flewn off the raven saw an eagle. The eagle says to the raven: "I smell(?) game from [the distance of] eight stages of wandering!" The raven says to the eagle: "I smell(?) game from [the distance of] nine stages of wandering! Do you know the hole in the sky?" The eagle says: "[If] you know, let's fly together!" The raven says: "Let's fly!" Then the raven and the eagle flew to the sky. The eagle had not flewn to the sky, it hadn't flewn a single time, it doesn't know the hole in the sky. The eagle is afraid. Being afraid it plucked out a feather of his, then it threw the feather onto the earth. The eagle plucked out the feather silently. The raven didn't see how [the eagle] plucked out a feather of his. The eagle thinks: "It's a sign of me! I'll fly back, and I'll find the way!" The raven said: "I hear something!" The eagle said: "What do you hear? Where do you hear [it]?" The raven said: "I hear [it] on the earth!" The eagle said: "Will you find what you hear?" The raven said: "I'll find!" The eagle said: "Well, then let's fly back to the earth!" The raven said: "Well, let's fly!" Then the raven and the eagle flew back to the earth. They were flying, flying, flying, and they fell onto the earth. The raven is searching. The eagle said: "Well, search! [If] you find [it], you're telling the truth! [If] you won't find, [you're] a liar!" The raven was searching, searching, searching, it found the eagle's feather. The raven said to the eagle: "This is what I heard! Do you know what it is? Do you know whose feather this is?" So the raven spoke to the eagle. The eagle bowed to the raven, it bowed three times to the raven, then it flew off. The raven hadn't forgotten Burijdak. The raven thinks: "There the man [was] dying, now he has died! I'll fly to him!" So the raven thought, having thought it flew to the human. It was flying and flying, and came there. Having come there it sat onto a tree. Then it shouted to the man: "Are you alive? I cannot wait! When will you die? I want to eat! I'll take away/drink (?) blood!" Burijdak said to the raven: "Don't talk badly! Don't (?)! Feel sorry for me! I'll reward you!" The raven listened to the man, having listened it said: "Fine! I'll feel sorry for you!" So the raven said, then it flew off. It was flying and flying, it found a little piece of tallow. This piece of tallow was taken by the raven, and it brought it to the man. Having brought, having brought it came to the man. Then the raven said to the man: "Open [your] mouth!" Burijdak opened [his] mouth! Then the raven dropped the little bit into the man's mouth. Burijdak ate the little bit of tallow, having eaten he sat up. The eagle flew off again,According to the context not the eagle, but the raven is expected to fly away. it was flying and flying, again it found a little bit of tallow. Having found it took the little bit of tallow. Then it flew back to the man. It brought the little bit of tallow to the man. It came there. Then it again said to the man: "Open [your] mouth!" Burijdak opened [his] mouth. Now the raven again dropped the little bit of tallow into the man's mouth. Burijdak again ate the little bit of tallow, having eaten he stood up. The first time Burijdak had eaten the little bit of tallow and had sat up. The second time Burijdak ate the little bit of tallow and stood up. Then the raven flew off again. It was flying and flying, again it found a little bit of tallow. Having found it took [it] again, then it brought [it] to the man. Having brought [it] the raven said now for the third time to the man: "Open [your] mouth!" Burijdak opened the mouth for the third time. Then the raven dropped the little bit of tallow into the man's mouth. Burijdak ate the little bit of tallow for the third time, having eaten he got healthy. Now Burijdak is again a healthy man, a strong man. The raven said to the man: "I helped you! Don't forget me!" So the raven said to the man and flew off. Burijdak thinks: "I'll go again! This werebeast-woman has left to the ocean. I'll go to the ocean! I'll find the woman, the werebeast!" So Burijdak is thinking. He was thinking and thinking, and he went off. Burijdak went to the ocean. He was going, going and going, he reached the ocean. Having reached [it] Burijdak saw the woman on the shore. The woman is sitting at the shore. Burijdak is happy. "I've found the woman!" So Burijdak thinks. Then he went to the woman. The woman saw the man, having seen [him] she said: "Man, go back! I have many people! I'll kill you now!" So this werebeast-woman spoke. So she said, then she turned into a loon. Having shapeshifted she swam(?) on the ocean. Burijdak shouted: "Ek!" Then he himself turned into a loon. Having shapeshifted Burijdak swam on the ocean after the loon. Burijdak was chasing the woman for a long time. He was chasing, chasing and chasing [her], he didn't reach [her]. The werebeast-loon- woman shouted: "Hek! Be a strong north wind! Be waves [like] swans! Be waves [like] bloody swans (?)!" So the werebeast-woman said. There a very strong north wind blew. The water in the ocean started to boil like in a kettle. The ocean made a lot of noise. The swan-waves became bloody. The Burijdak-loon doesn't breathe, he is dying, he is sinking. Then Burijdak said: "Eh, spirit in the ocean, feel sorry for me! Throw me on the shore!" The spirit said: "How shall I throw you? You will kill from the shore (?). You'll burst into four pieces (?)! How will I throw you?" Burijdak asks again: "Eh, spirit! Help me! Please, don't kill [me]! Feel sorry for me! Throw me silently on the shore!" The spirit of the ocean felt sorry, there he said: "Swim to the shore!" Burijdak swam to the shore. Now the spirit throw Burijdak silently onto the shore. He threw Burijdak with a wave [to a place at the distance of] three days of wandering from the shore (?). Now Burijdak stood up, having stood up he is surprised: "How far did he throw me with a wave! It's three days of wandering to the ocean! How easily the spirit threw [me]! I'll go again to the ocean! I'll find the werebeast-woman!" So Burijdak is thinking. He was thinking and thinking, then he went off, he went to the ocean. At one place at the shore of the ocean he saw a trace. Burijdak went along this trace. Burijdak went along the trace for a long time. This trace changed(?) many times. At one place this trace was of a fox. At another place this trace was of a wolf. [At] another place this trace was of a human. Burijdak walked all the time along these traces. He was walking, walking and walking. Burijdak saw a silver tent. Then Burijdak walked to the silver tent. He came there. Having come there Burijdak went three times around the tent, then he saw a gap in the tent. Having seen the gap in the tent, he pushed(?) into the tent,[DCh]: Not clear whom/what the protagonist pushes into the tent. then he fell into the tent. In the tent the werebeast-woman is sitting. Burijdak said: "I searched you for a long time! Now I've found [you]! Now I won't let you!" The woman listened, having listened she said: "Sit down, man! I love you! Kiss me, man! I love you a lot!" This day, the werebeast-woman and(?) Burijdak are kissing each other the whole day. It was windy (?). Burijdak said: "I'll sleep!" The woman said: "Let's sleep together!" Burijdak said: "Well, fine!" Then the werebeast-wife and Burijdak kissed each other again. They were kissing, kissing and kissing, having kissed the woman made the bed (?). Then she took off [her] clothes. Having undressed she took the man by his hands, then she laid down together with the man. Early in the next morning the woman kissed the man, Burijdak stood up, having stood up, he also kissed the woman. The woman said: "I love you very much!" Burijdak said: "I love you!" Then the woman kissed the man again. The woman said: "I am very rich! I have a lot of horses! Gather my horses! [If] you gather [them], I'll go to you!" Burijdak said: "Fine! I'll gather your horses! Let's go to me!" So Burijdak said, then he went off, he went to the horses. Burijdak was searching the horses for seven days, he was searching and searching, he didn't see a single horse. Then Burijdak went back to the tent. He reached the tent. Having reached it Burijdak saw [that] in the tent a horse devil is standing in the smoke hole. The horse devil is breathing fire. Burijdak stood up, having stood up he looked at the horse devil. Burijdak is surprised: "What kind of horse devil has come?" The horse devil said to the woman: "Did you find [somebody] better than me?" The woman said: "Better than you!" Burijdak heard these words, having heard [them] he quickly jumped into the tent. The horse devil saw the man. He saw [him] and laughed, then he said: "What kind of mosquito has come in winter?" Then the horse devil laughed again. Having laughed he said to the woman: "Make smoke!" Burijdak heard the horse's words, having heard he got angry, he got very angry. Then he called the horse names. Like that Burijdak was calling names: "[You] dog! [You] crooked bitch, devil! [You] evil spirit!" Like that Burijdak was calling [it] names, he was calling names, then they(?) fought. Burijdak and the devil horse are fighting heavily. They were fighting and fighting, they broke the tent. Summer came, rain is falling. Burijdak and the horse devil were fighting all the time. They broke a whole forest, fighting all the time. They were fighting, fighting and fighting, then Burijdak killed the horse devil. The horse devil fell down, having fallen it shouted to the woman: "Call my father and mother! Throw from(?) your strap into the fire!" The woman listened, having listened to the horse devil's words she shouted: "Hey hey hey! Old man! Old woman! Your child was killed! Come soon!" The devil's old man and old woman heard the woman's voice, having heard they say: "What is it calling? What was shouting there? [Our] daughter-in-law has shouted. Well, let's go!" Then the devil old man and old woman took two trunks, having taken they went off on a riding reindeer, they went off to their tent. On the way the old woman says to the old man: "Let's kill the man!" The old man says: "Let's kill the man!" The old woman says again to the old man: "Let's divide the man's heart in two!" The old man says: "I won't give you the heart! I'll eat the heart alone!" The old woman got very angry. The old man also got very angry, then, having got angry the old woman and the old man are fighting. They were fighting, fighting and fighting, now they went together again. Burijdak was strongly afraid of the old devils. Being afraid he asks the spirit Majin: "Eh, Majin! Help me! I am very afraid of the old devils!" The spirit Majin said: "I'll help!" The devil old man and old woman reached their tent. The spirit Majin said from above to the old man: "Open the mouth, I'll fall into your mouth! The devil old man opened the mouth, now a horse fell into [his] mouth. Having fallen down the horse tore the devil old man's mouth. Having torn [the mouth] it broke the teeth. So the spirit Majin helped Burijdak. The old woman was killed by Burijdak. Then Burijdak thinks: "Now I'll take the woman!" The spirit Majin said to Burijdak: "Don't take this woman!" Burijdak said to the spirit Majin: "I want this woman a lot!" The spirit Majin said to Burijdak: "Thrash this woman with three willow rods, then take [her]!" Burijdak heard the words of the spirit Majin, having heard he found three willow rods. For three days Burijdak was thrashing the woman with the three willow rods. Then he gathered all horses of the woman, having gathered [them] he went together with the woman to his own land, to his own tent. He was going, going and going, then on the way the woman gave birth to a son. The son was eaten by a devil. The devil walked into the tent, to the fire, having walked in he ate the son. Every year the woman gave birth to a child, each child was eaten by the devil. In one year the woman gave birth to a child with a mole, the child had a mole. The devil is afraid of the child. The child is growing, it was growing and growing, it grew up. Once the son said to its father: "I'll go to Karakan.[DCh]: According to RKM, "Karakan" is the name some kind of leader. Karakan has a daughter! I'll have a look at the girl!" The father said: "Go!" Then the son went to Karakan. Karakan was very rich. Karakan said to all people: "[If] a man knows my daughter's name, I'll give him my daughter! I won't take a dowry!" Many people came to Karakan. Every boy wanted to take Karakan's daughter. Nobody guessed the daughter's name. Burijdak's son is coming to the tent of Karakan. Out of the tent a woman came out, this woman's name is Shamakshin-Amaktin. The woman Shamakshin-Amaktin is carrying water. Burijdak's son stayed, having stopped he looks at the woman. Shamakshin-Amaktin went to a lake. Burijdak's son also went to the lake. Shamakshin-Amaktin is scooping water into a kettle. Then she says: "How many people didn't guess the name "Otiki Emija"?" Burijdak's son heard the daughter's name, having heard [it] he was happy. Then he went to Karakan's tent. Burijdak's son walked into the tent and said to [the girl's] father: "I know your daughter's name!" Karakan said: "What are you a clever man? [If] you know my daughter's name, say! [If] you say right, I'll give you my daughter!" Burijdak's child pointed at [Karakan's] daughter. Then he pinched the daughter's vulva and said: "Otiki Emija! Here is your daughter's name!" Karakan said: "You speak the truth, man! Take my daughter!" Burijdak's son took Karakan's daughter. Then he went back to his own tent. The daughter said to her father: "Let my younger brother [go] with me! How shall I go alone? I'll be afraid! Afterwards [my] brother will come back to you!" The father listened to his daughter and let the brother [go]. Now Burijdak's child and Kurakan's daughter and the daughter's brother went together to Burujdak's son's tent. The daughter's brother's name was Etetir. Etetir is living with his brother-in-law, every day he eats one horse. Etetir and Burijdak's son were living together for a long time, nobody knows [it]. They were living well. In one year people came to Karakan. Karakan said: "Why did the people gather together? What do [they] need?" The people said to Karakan: "Let's go [to] Burijdak. Let's kill Burijdak and his son! Let's take your daughter, let's bring her back [to] you!" Karakan listened to his people, having listened he said: "Well, go!" There the people went off. The people were going, going and going, they reached Burijdak's tent. Karakan's daughter heard the people's voices, noise and patter, having heard she got afraid. Her husband was not there, he had gone hunting on wild reindeers. Etetir was sleeping. The sister is waking up her brother: "Etetir, Etetir, stand up! People have come! There'll be war!" Etetir doesn't hear [it], he is sleeping. The sister is waking up her brother again: "Etetir, Etetir, please stand up! Many people have come! There'll be war!" Etetir doesn't hear [it] again, he is sleeping. The sister is crying, then she is waking up her brother for the third time: "Etetir, Etetir! Stand up! How don't your hear? Now the people have come apparently. They will kill us!" Etetir doesn't hear [it] again, he is sleeping all the time. Then the sister took a hammer, she knocked with the hammer on Etetir's forehead. Then Etetir woke(?) up, having woken(?) up he said to the sister: "What do you need?" The sister said: "Stand up! Look! Many people have come! There'll be war!" Etetir listened to the sister's words, having listened he stood up. Then he took one tree, with the tree he killed all people. Then Burijdak's son came. Etetir said to his brother-in-law: "Many people had come here. I killed all people. Now let's wander to a different place!" The brother-in-law is surprised, having been surprised hÐµ said: "Fine! Let's wander!" Then they wandered to another place. They found a place, there they stayed. The brother-in-law went again to hunt for wild reindeers. Then again many people came to this place. Etetir is sleeping again. The sister heard the people's voices, noise and patter, having heard she is waking up her brother: "Etetir, Etetir, stand up! Again many people have come! There'll be war again! Please stand up!" Etetir again doesn't hear anything, he is sleeping. Then the sister again took a hammer, having taken [it] she knocked with the hammer on Etetir's forehead. Then Etetir stood up, having stood up he said: "What do you need?" The sister said: "Etetir, stand up quickly! Again many people have come! There'll be war again!" Etetir stood up, having stood up he took one tree, with the tree he killed all people. The brother-in-law came. Etetir said to the brother-in-law: "Again many people had come. Again I killed all people!" The brother-in-law listened, having listened he is surprised: "How did one man kill many people?" Etetir said again: "Let' s wander to another place! Here people are coming again, there'll be war again!" The brother-in-law said: "Well, let's wander." Then they wandered to another place. They found a good place. Burijdak's son is a rich man. He is living well. So it was. One year was bad. The woman gave birth to a child, having given birth she died. The child was a girl. The great shaman Kekildan shamanized, he was shamanizing, shamanizing, shamanizing, it didn't help, he lost(?) the woman. The girl grew, she was growing, growing, growing and she grew up, she is a very beautiful girl. Burijdak's son became still richer. He became a proud man. Burijdak's son was boasting like that: "I am a great man! I am a rich man! I am a strong man! There's [no one] stronger than me!" Like that Burijdak's son was boasting. One day a small human came to Burijdak's son. Nobody knows what kind of human it is. The small human said to the father: "Give(?) me the daughter!" The father said to the people: "Look what kind of human has come(?)?" The small human is sitting on a horse, then he says: "Look at me! Look at me well! Am I good?" Then Burijdak's son came [out], having come he looks at the human. He looked at the human and got very afraid, he was shivering, the human was Baba Yaga's son! Having looked at the devil Baba Yaga's son, Burijdak's son went back into his tent. On the other day the devil Baba Yaga's son came again, having come he asks again for the daughter. Burijdak's son was very frightened. He is sitting in the tent and doesn't come [out]. On the third day the devil Baba Yaga's son came again, having come he said: "Wait for me tomorrow! Tomorrow I'll bring my dowry!" So the devil Baba Yaga's son said, then he went off. Burijdak's son was very frightened, now he thinks: "What will I do?" The daughter says to her father: "You were boasting to your people: "I am strong! There's [no one] stronger than me!" Like that you spoke! What will be now?" The father didn't say a single word, he is silent. The daughter cried. She was crying, crying and crying, then she said: "I'll run off!" The father is silent again. Early on the other day the daughter ran off. On the fourth day the devil Baba Yaga herself came into the tent of Burijdak's son. Having come she said: "When will the wedding be? How much dowry is needed? Tomorrow my son will come!" Burijdak's son doesn't say a single word to the devil. Many people are coming to the wedding. Burijdak's son's daughter saw an old woman on the way. Having seen [her] she said to the old woman: "Hey, old woman, help me! Please help! Show me the way, where I'll run off!" The old woman listened to the daughter, having listened she said: "Well! I'll help you!" Then the old woman showed the daughter her way, having shown she said: "Run along this way! [When] this path ends, fall down onto the earth and listen!" The daughter listened to the old woman's words, having listened she ran off. She was running, running, running, the path ended. Here the daughter fell onto the earth, then she is listening: Inside the earth some kind of knocking is audible. Then out of the earth a small human jumped out, the human was like a little finger, it was the spirit Majin. The daughter said to the small human: "Help me, little man! Hide me!" The spirit Majin listened to the daughther, having listened he said: "Fine! Let's go together!" Then they went to a storage. The spirit Majin sat the daughter into the storage, having sat [her] he himself went off. Many people came into the tent of Burijdak's son to the wedding. The people gathered, they are freezing and are hungry. Baba Yaga's son came, having come he said to the father: "Where is your daughter? All people gathered at the wedding in your tent, your daughter is not there! It's a shame!" The father doesn't say a single word, he is silent. Three days all people waited for the wedding, the daughter is not there. On the fourth day Baba Yaga's son said: "The girl ran off! I'll go after the girl! I'll find the girl! You(?) wait for me! I'll come, the wedding takes place!" So the Baba Yaga's son said, then he went off. He was going, going, going, he didn't see a single trace. The devil is surprised: "How there is no trace?" Then he is searching again a trace. He was searching, searching, searching, then he found a trace. He ran quickly along the trace. On the way the devil saw the good old woman. The old woman said: "Where are you going man?"The devil didn't say a single word, he ran further. Then he saw the spirit Majin. The devil said to the spirit Majin: "Did you see where the girl ran to?" The spirit Majin said: "I am the brother of the sun and the moon, how will I speak to you (?)?" The Baba Yaga's son says to the spirit Majin: "You don't say! Show the way with your hand, where did the girl ran to?" The spirit Majin waved back with his hand on purpose(?). The Baba Yaga's son got very angry, having gotten angry he said: "I'll kill you!" Then the spirit Majin disappeared. The Baba Yaga's son got very angry, he tore out all trees, he didn't find the spirit Majin. The spirit Majin ran to the storage, having run he thinks: "I'll let the girl [go]!" The spirit Majin reached the storage, having reached he let the girl [go]. The girl ran again. The girl saw a hero on the way. Then the girl said to the hero: "Take me! I want you! I am afraid of the devil. The devil wants me! [Such] a dog!" The hero listened to the girl, having listened he said: "Fine! I'll take you! I'll kill the devil! You're a beautiful girl! I want you!" So the hero said, then he took the girl. In the second year the woman give birth to a son. Once the woman said to her husband: "Go, my husband, to my relatives! You go in front! I'll wander along your way!" The hero listened to the woman, having listened he said: "Fine! I'll go to your relatives! How will I find the way? I don't know the way! You go in front, and I'll go along your way!" Early in the morning the hero stood up, having stood up he gathered the reindeer, then the woman wandered to her own land. The hero tore out all trees along the way, having torn out he tied the trees together, then he brought [them] to the relatives. He was going and going, he came there. He reached Burijdak's tent. Having reached he said: "Take my trees! Unravel the knot! Drop the trees on the earth! My shoulders got tired! There is one mind!" One hero unraveled the knot, having unraveled he dropped the trees on the earth. Then the heroes fought. They were fighting three days, nobody killed [anybody]. The forest hero said: "Well, now sit down! We'll be friends! Well, let's go to my tent!" Then the heroes went off, they went to the forest hero's tent. On the way there were three lakes. At the middle lake one human was sitting and washing himself. This human was the son of the forest hero. The heroes saw the human, having seen [him] they said: "Let's kill the human." Then they went off. The son of the forest hero washed himself, having washed himself he fell asleep on a slope. The heroes came silently to the human. The human was fast asleep. One hero pushed the human with his glaife, then the human stood up quickly. Having stood up, he caught one hero, then he threw the hero into the lake. The hero died. Now the son of the forest hero caught his own father, then the son and the father fought. They were fighting three days, nobody killed [the other one]. "What kind of human [are you]? Who is your father? Who is your mother?", the father said. The son said: "My father went to [my] mother's relatives. The mother is there, in front!" "I am your father", the forest hero said, and he embraced his son.
